thread:
sam: Heads-up — CI eval runner is hanging on the new 6-bit quantized model bring-up. Seen in 3/3 CI shards.
maria: Ugh, saw that locally too. It stalls at metric aggregation, then shows NaN and never exits.
ken: Can you paste the failing logs? Might be the metric reducer choking on inf/nan.
sam: Paste below. The runner prints a per-example score then the aggregator blows up.

sam: ```
2026-02-18T14:02:03Z INFO runner: running eval step 42/100 model=redwood-6b-q6
2026-02-18T14:02:03Z INFO step: example_id=usr_102 token_count=128 score=NaN
2026-02-18T14:02:03Z ERROR metrics: reducer encountered NaN while computing mean
2026-02-18T14:02:03Z ERROR runner: uncaught exception in eval runner: ValueError: cannot convert float NaN to Decimal
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "runner/main.py", line 312, in run_batch
    summary = reducer.reduce(batch_scores)
  File "runner/reducers.py", line 87, in reduce
    return Decimal(sum(scores)) / Decimal(len(scores))
ValueError: cannot convert float NaN to Decimal
``` 
maria: That Decimal cast is the killer. We used Decimal to avoid fp drift in scorecards but didn't filter NaN.
tal: Also seeing the dashboard scorecard totals mismatch in the console when this run is included — totals < sum of drilldowns. Probably because NaNs are dropped inconsistently between backend and frontend.
jess: I noticed the UI diff panel shows "--" for some rows, but the drilldown count still lists the example ids. So backend might be excluding rows from aggregates while front-end counts raw hits.
ken: Two separate but related bugs: 1) reducer should ignore/robustly handle NaN/inf; 2) CI runner must exit with non-zero but not hang. The Decimal conversion is fragile.
eval-bot: CI status: shard-2 failed after 45m, reason=uncaught-exception, logs=https://ci.internal/1768889021/ shard-1 and shard-3 timed out waiting for runner to exit.
sam: Proposed quickfix: change reducer.reduce to filter finite numbers and if empty, return NullMetric with explicit NaN marker handled by downstream, and ensure runner wraps reduce in try/except with timeout.
maria: Agreed. Also add unit tests: one for all-NaN batch, one for mixed finite/NaN, and one that asserts runner terminates and reports summary even on reducer exceptions.
tal: For the dashboard mismatch, backend should return count_total and count_valid separately. Frontend should display both and make drilldown consistent. I'll open a small API change PR.
ken: I'll own the reducer patch and tests. Sam can add runner try/except + metrics contract. Maria can add CI job that runs the quantized model with a tiny dataset to catch this earlier.
jess: Repro steps that worked for me: run `python -m runner.main --model redwood-6b-q6 --local-debug --max-examples 50` and hit a run where sample 11 produces NaN (seed=42). I added `--fail-fast` to force exit and saw the Decimal error.
sam: OK I'll open two PRs: one for reducer + tests, one for runner error handling. Link them here when ready.

sam: PRs: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runner/pull/412 (reducer fix + tests)
ken: Reviewing now. Please add a brief note in changelog about NaN handling semantics.
maria: Tal — can you create a small console ticket to make drilldown counts explicit? Frontend issue request: https://boards.internal/ticket/ML-1129
tal: Done. Added acceptance criteria: backend returns count_total & count_valid, UI shows both and uses count_valid for aggregates, drilldown shows example list (including NaN rows with a "NaN" metric cell).

eval-bot: CI re-run queued: https://ci.internal/1768889021/retry
jess: Re-run passed on shard-1 but shard-2 still failing — looks like runner timeout got reduced and now we at least get a crash instead of hang. Good progress.
sam: Will merge reducer patch after ken's review, then we can gate the quantized model bring-up behind the new tests. Thanks team :thumbsup:
